rv.q: It is one of the best plays you’ll ever see.
One reason Jerusalem was and remains so remarkable is that it is so different from the boring compliance of most other new drama.
Together, this exemplary ensemble give us a breath-taking portrait of backwater England that roves from the profane to the sublime, a crucial theatrical rite, fit for the ages.
For a few months, it has returned to our dark, satanic mills.
With Rylance in the role, its spell is irresistible.
Rylance’s Rooster is surely the greatest performance of the century.
It is quite simply just wondrous.
Butterworth’s infinitely rich play is proof that legends age well.
In a thrilling revival that opened Thursday at the Apollo Theater, everything feels enriched by time.
Wild and whimsical, uproarious and desolate, Butterworth’s play is still a mighty force of irrepressible live theatre.

This brilliant, highly topical three-hour twenty-minute play, that seems to pass very quickly, takes us through his nine-hour day with the outcasts and the escapees from the dull life of the world beyond the forest.

cn.t: Critics hail this revival as potent proof of the play's modern masterpiece status, with Rylance's "titanic," award-winning return as Rooster Byron described as superhuman. A few dissenters question the hype, but most find it gloriously intact.
